title: MOSS: Multi-Objective Optimization for Stable Rule Sets

problem.claim: Constructing interpretable rule sets requires balancing sparsity, predictive accuracy, and stability.

contributions.claim: MOSS is a multi-objective optimization framework for constructing stable decision-rule sets.
The framework jointly incorporates sparsity, accuracy, and stability and enables evaluation of the accuracy–stability trade-off.
A specialized cutting-plane algorithm computes the Pareto frontier between accuracy and stability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithm scales to problem instances beyond the capabilities of commercial optimization solvers.
The authors report that MOSS outperforms state-of-the-art rule ensembles in predictive performance and stability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces MOSS for constructing stable decision-rule sets.
Combines sparsity, accuracy, and stability to expose model trade-offs.
Uses a specialized cutting-plane algorithm to compute the accuracy–stability Pareto frontier.
Reports scalability beyond commercial solvers and improved predictive performance and stability over rule ensembles.

source_observation.claim: The framework represents interpretability through multiple jointly optimized criteria rather than a single objective.

interpretation.claim: When interpretability dimensions conflict, exposing their Pareto trade-off can support model selection.

application.claim: Use multi-objective evaluation when selecting sparse rule-based models under competing accuracy and stability requirements.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these lessons generalize beyond the reported problem instances or rule-ensemble comparisons.

unknowns: Datasets, data sizes, and experimental settings are not specified.
Definitions and measurement procedures for stability, sparsity, and predictive performance are not specified.
The reported comparison metrics and statistical significance are not specified.
